name: Steamed rice rolls
summary: Cao Bang bánh cuốn is a steamed rice sheet eaten hot in pork-bone broth. The 4 July 2012 article says stalls open from 4 to 5 in the morning. A closing time and a price are Check on arrival.
howToEat: Báo Cao Bằng on 4 July 2012: local ordinary rice, soaked and wet-milled, filled with pork that is minced and fried with dried shallot, then eaten hot in a clear pork-bone broth with gio, cha, and egg. Chili pickled with mắc mật, fish sauce, and lime are optional. An egg cracked into the sheet while it steams is that article’s egg roll.
The 1 September 2026 article says the roll is not eaten with the familiar fish sauce. It describes a white hot sheet, bone broth, minced pork, scallion, and pickled bamboo chili.
Stalls open from 4 to 5 in the morning on the 4 July 2012 article. A closing time and a price are Check on arrival.
where: Morning stalls in Cao Bang city. The 4 July 2012 article says almost every street had a stall. The Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism on 22 August 2024 says bánh cuốn Cao Bằng was chosen for a top 100 Vietnamese dish list.

texture: Báo Cao Bằng on 4 July 2012 says the sheet is chewy and soft. The 1 September 2026 article says the sheet is white, soft, and hot.
